Following [Working with us](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/docs/working-with-us.md#step-0-create-an-extension), the same behavior is available today as an extension: [mrecachinas/gh-verify-download](https://github.com/mrecachinas/gh-verify-download) (`gh extension install mrecachinas/gh-verify-download`).

### Description

Before running a downloaded release asset, it's worth knowing whether the release is immutable and how the asset was built. `gh` can check this today, but only after downloading and across several commands, so people rarely do.

`gh release download --verify` runs these checks **before** downloading and then asks whether to continue:

- **Immutable releases:** GitHub's signed release attestation must verify, match this release, and list each asset's name and digest.
- **Build provenance:** each asset's SLSA attestation must be signed by GitHub Actions and built from the release's repository. The workflow, commit, ref, and run are shown.
- **After downloading**, each file must match its expected sha256.

In a terminal the prompt defaults to *No* if anything failed; non-interactive runs fail instead. A release asset URL can also be passed in place of a tag.

### How did you test this change?

I built this branch and ran it against public releases.

An immutable, attested release downloads after showing its provenance:

```
$ gh release download --verify https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v2.102.1/gh_2.102.1_macOS_arm64.zip
cli/cli v2.102.1
✓ Immutable release, verified by GitHub's signed release attestation

gh_2.102.1_macOS_arm64.zip
✓ Listed in the signed release attestation
✓ Verified SLSA build provenance
  - Build instructions: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/89d7dcec017194af1d6f8853176b2dae9c1da762/.github/workflows/deployment.yml
  - Source:             https://github.com/cli/cli/tree/89d7dcec017194af1d6f8853176b2dae9c1da762
  - Source ref:         refs/heads/bagtoad/go-1-27-3-patch-on-v2-102-0
  - Build run:          https://github.com/cli/cli/actions/runs/39482998765/attempts/1
  - Runner:             github-hosted
```

A mutable release without attestations is refused (exit 1, nothing written). In a terminal I instead saw `? Download mockery_2.53.8_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz? (y/N)`.

```
$ gh release download --verify https://github.com/vektra/mockery/releases/download/v2.53.8/mockery_2.53.8_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
vektra/mockery v2.53.8
! Not an immutable release; assets can be replaced after publishing

mockery_2.53.8_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
X No build provenance attestation found

refusing to download: 1 asset failed verification; run without `--verify` to download anyway
```

I also saw that `-O -` writes the verified bytes (piping to `shasum -a 256` gave the attested `08bfef98…aa2aeb`), and that GHES hosts and `--archive` are rejected up front with an explanation.

### Key points

- Assets are downloaded to a private temp directory and checked there; they're only written to the destination (or stdout) if every asset passes. A failed check leaves existing files untouched.
- Provenance may be signed by any Actions workflow on the host (so reusable workflows work), but the source repository is pinned, matching `gh attestation verify --repo`.
- Mutable releases only warn, since they have no release attestation; build provenance decides.
- Without `--verify`, an asset literally named `-` is now saved as a file rather than streamed to stdout.

### Notes for reviewers

Start with `pkg/cmd/release/download/provenance.go` (`confirmProvenance`, `check`, `checkRelease`), then `downloadVerified` in `download.go`. It reuses the existing attestation client, Sigstore verifier, and `shared.AttestationVerifier`.

Open questions: should this be a flag or its own command, and should mutable releases with valid provenance pass silently in scripts?
